After more than a decade without a touchscreen display in its laptop lineup, Apple is finally set to launch its first touchscreen MacBook as early as October. The new machine will debut alongside the next-generation MacBook Pro redesign and may be named the MacBook Ultra.

Of course, rumours are just rumours — but almost every credible source agrees that the MacBook Pro will gain touch support later this year. Apple has even left a few hints in macOS 27: Sidecar touch support, pull-to-refresh functionality, and slightly enlarged menu bar items.

As a 13-inch MacBook Air user, that last one is particularly annoying to me, because things that used to fit on the left side of the notch now spill beyond it.

You could call these coincidences, but they look very much like part of a deliberate plan. Either way, here's what the first touchscreen MacBook will offer.

OLED, Dynamic Island

On the display front, the redesigned MacBook Pro will feature a Tandem OLED panel similar to the iPad Pro, which is widely regarded as one of the best mobile displays on the market. Tandem OLED consists of stacked OLED layers that deliver better colour, higher contrast and greater brightness.

Reports also say the new machine will come with a Dynamic Island, slightly smaller than the one on iPhone, but without Face ID support.

Software Optimisations

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple will introduce a number of special optimisations for the first touchscreen MacBook Pro that go beyond what's already visible in the macOS 27 beta:

"For example, if a user touches a button or control, the interface will pop up a new kind of menu around their finger, offering options that are more suited to touch commands. The software will also display the most appropriate combination of controls based on the user's past interactions. When the user taps an item in the menu bar at the top of the screen, the control combinations will enlarge, making it easier to pick with a finger."

M5 Pro and M5 Max Chips

Although early reports suggested the redesigned MacBook Pro would debut with the M6 Pro and Max chips, Apple has now decided to skip the release of those two chips and push ahead with M7 development. In other words, the redesigned MacBook Pro will not use the first batch of 2nm chips, but will instead stick with the current M5 Pro and M5 Max.

However, the laptop will not have a base-model version for now, though rumours suggest Apple may launch a base-model redesigned MacBook Pro with an M7 chip as early as next spring.

Slightly Thinner Body

One of the design rumours for the new MacBook Pro is a slightly thinner and lighter chassis, though it's unclear what that change really means in practice. The previous MacBook Pro looked and felt quite chunky, so any improvement here would likely be welcome — as long as it doesn't come at the cost of thermal performance.

Summary

Overall, the first touchscreen MacBook Pro looks like an exciting upgrade. Because Apple raised prices in June due to the memory crisis, this machine will be even more expensive — with the 14-inch expected to start at US$2,499 and the 16-inch at US$2,999.

Are you excited about a touchscreen MacBook? Will you buy one the moment it launches, or wait for the cheaper 14-inch base model? Share your thoughts in the comments.
